tier.instructions: You do NOT answer the request. Decide only WHO in a home AI lab should handle this ONE request.

criteria.tool: a lab tool or plain code does it: make, render or generate an image or photo; re-render one with a change; wake or reboot a machine; check a job's, a render's or a machine's progress, status or rate; approve or propose a lab action; run a named lab tool; look up who can be rendered
criteria.fellowship: simple chat a tiny model answers instantly from general knowledge: a greeting, small talk, a one-line fact anyone knows (a number, a date, a name, the year, a definition), a ping
criteria.8gb: a short answer that needs the lab's OWN documentation or records looked up: where something is in the lab, why something was decided, what a lab component does, a brief summary of a lab document
criteria.lead: real work or anything needing judgment: coding, multi-step research, writing help, plans and designs, reviewing documents or code, finding things on a machine, legal or other high-stakes reasoning - and ANY request you are unsure about

family.instructions: Which family of work is this request?

criteria.ops: ops (running the lab's machines and services)

kind.instructions: Is this request a chat or a job?

criteria.chat: answered in one reply, at most one tool call
criteria.job: many steps, tools, or work that runs as an order

depth.instructions: You do NOT answer the request. Decide only HOW the user wants it handled: a QUICK reply right now, or a THOROUGH piece of work they expect to wait for.

criteria.quick: the user wants a fast, short reply now: a fact, a number, a yes or no, a quick explanation, small talk, a status check - anything they would be annoyed to wait more than a few seconds for
criteria.deep: the user is asking for real work and expects to wait for it: analysis, research, a plan or design, writing or generating something, reviewing documents or code, a multi-step task, anything that needs reading or tools first
